name: New York
agency: New York State Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 15 after sunset, certified by a parent or guardian on form MV-262 brought to each road test
teen.holdPermit: 6 months before the road test (NYS Health GDL parent guide)
teen.nightLimit: Junior license: no unsupervised driving 9 p.m. to 5 a.m. except listed trips (home to work, school course, etc.); no driving in New York City at all. Learner permit: never in NYC 9 p.m. to 5 a.m.
teen.passengerLimit: Junior license without supervisor: no more than one passenger under 21 who is not immediate family. Junior permit: no front-seat passenger except the supervisor.
teen.phone: Junior permit or license (DJ/MJ): first cell phone or texting conviction = 120-day suspension; second within six months of restoration = revocation of at least one year

notes: Written test (DMV Chapter 1): 20 questions, at least 14 correct and at least 2 of the 4 road sign questions. Online test page states 80 percent overall and 50 percent of sign questions; the two rules differ.
Class D test offered in 20 languages including Spanish (DMV permit test page).
Supervisor must be 21 or older with a valid license for the vehicle type. In NYC, permit driving in daytime only in a dual-control car.
Most new drivers need a 5-hour pre-licensing course (MV-278) unless they complete a high school or college driver education course.
School bus: stop in both directions, divided highways included; stay at least 20 feet back (DMV Chapter 6, School Bus Safety).
No right turn on red in New York City unless a sign allows it (DMV Chapter 4).
Headlights required whenever wipers are needed for weather; daytime running lights do not count (DMV Chapter 10).
Speed limit 55 mph when none is posted; 25 mph in New York City unless posted; some rural expressways posted 65 (DMV Chapter 8).
Move Over law enacted 2010, expanded 2023 to all vehicles stopped on the roadway (GTSC).
Search budget for this state (5) fully used; no official page was fetched directly. Figures come from search summaries of official dmv.ny.gov pages.
